purpose: Two corrections to the evidence base, no verdict claimed and no code changed. First: V6.1.1 asks the documentation to make clear how anti-automation controls PREVENT malicious account lockout, and measurement shows they do not - the finding is recorded rather than papered over. Second: V8.2.4 silently stopped being evaluated between builds because an unrelated privacy merge made one of its absence patterns match; the condition is repaired so the requirement is under observation again.
requiredInvariants: No verdict is claimed as PASS by this pass. V6.1.1 and V6.3.1 stay FAIL; V8.2.4 returns from NOT_ASSESSED to FAIL, which raises the FAIL count from 89 to 90 because that is the honest number - NOT_ASSESSED there was not a better state, it was the absence of observation.

No application code is touched. The login lockout is measured and written down, not changed: keying the counter by account and IP needs a schema change to auth.login_throttles and is a trade-off against distributed password spraying, so it is the owner's decision.

The enumeration resistance already present must not be lost in any later fix: a non-existent address is treated exactly like an existing one and also accumulates failures. That is deliberate, and re-keying the throttle must preserve it.

The repaired V8.2.4 patterns detect what a real geolocation control would use, never a mention of the word. All seven are verified absent from the tree, and the PostHog disable flag that broke the old pattern deliberately does not match.

No dependency, schema, migration, RLS or policy change. No registration business logic, 1C, marketing or presentation code. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Login lockout measured exactly: auth.login_throttles is keyed by account_hash = hash('account:' + email) with no IP component; MAX_FAILED_LOGINS = 5; LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MS = 15 minutes; the login route is rate limited per IP at 8 per 60 seconds. Five requests lock a known address for fifteen minutes, and roughly twenty requests an hour from one address hold it locked. Knowing the address is enough; the password is not needed.

V8.2.4 drift diagnosed to its cause: the absence pattern 'geoip' began matching '$geoip_disable': true, introduced by the privacy-bounded PostHog merge - a flag that turns geolocation OFF. A substring check cannot tell use from disablement.

The repair is falsifiable in both directions, proven by mutation: introducing a real maxmind lookup drives the verdict to NOT_ASSESSED for re-assessment, while the PostHog disable flag alone leaves it FAIL.
Matrix against current main c725f6af4: exactly one verdict changes, V8.2.4 NOT_ASSESSED -> FAIL. PASS 129, FAIL 90, NOT_APPLICABLE 88, NOT_ASSESSED 38.
